_doc: The 1904 Prairie Avenue street surfaces (T-1728): what each carriageway, alley and sidewalk band of data/street_grid/1904.json (T-0474) was made of on 1 July 1904, with a tier, the sources, and a date range the scene date falls inside. AUTHORED -- edit by hand; tools/check_street_surfaces.py --check holds it to the grid, the sources, the liberties and the texture library. The grid owns the geometry; this file owns only materials. Research: docs/RESEARCH/prairie_1904_street_surfaces.md.
evidence_rule: A block's surface is ATTESTED only where a record names it for that block on both sides of the scene date or names it worn and out of guaranty after it; INFERRED where a record orders or lets it and nothing confirms it was laid; RECONSTRUCTED otherwise, with a liberty. The 1904 paving report (alvord_street_paving_report_1904, the Prairie library's civic-paving-1904) and the 1905 code only BOUND the reconstructed choices.
bounding_only_note: The 1904 paving report and the 1905 code name what a Chicago street, walk or curb could be made of; neither names a block of this grid. They bound reconstructed surfaces and can never attest one (tools/check_street_surfaces.py holds it).

authority.in_1904: City of Chicago: the Board of Local Improvements paved by special assessment, the Department of Public Works repaired
authority.note: The 1911 Sanborn sheets' 'Prairie Av. Blvd.' and 'E. 16th St. (Boulevard)' are the South Park Commissioners' boulevard, which the city consented to on 28 May 1904 and again on 30 October 1905 and the Commissioners took on 24 October 1906. On the scene date both were city streets.

sheet_asphalt.name: sheet asphalt
sheet_asphalt.what: lake asphalt and sand laid hot over a concrete base, rolled smooth
sheet_asphalt.bound_note: One of the six permanent pavements the code names (sec. 1944); 132 of Chicago's 1,371 miles at 1 January 1904, and the one Alvord's report recommends for 'high-class residence streets with considerable traffic'.

macadam.name: macadam (crushed limestone)
macadam.what: broken limestone rolled and bound with its own dust and water
macadam.bound_note: 421 of the city's 1,371 miles at 1 January 1904 (Alvord p. 26); the Board of Local Improvements' specifications of 1902 build it of slag, crushed limestone and crushed granite in courses.

vitrified_brick.name: vitrified paving brick
vitrified_brick.what: hard-burned paving brick laid on edge on a sand bed
vitrified_brick.bound_note: 68 miles in 1904 (Alvord p. 26); 'some of it has been laid on high-class residence streets, where its noise has not made it popular'.

earth_and_cinders.name: graded earth and cinders (unimproved)
earth_and_cinders.what: the natural ground graded and dressed with ashes and cinders
earth_and_cinders.bound_note: An alley no paving record reaches. Alvord counts 1,371 miles of IMPROVED streets and alleys against more than 1,900 miles of water pipe, i.e. a great deal of unimproved way.

portland_cement_walk.name: Portland cement concrete walk, 5 x 6 ft blocks
portland_cement_walk.what: cement concrete on a cinder bed with a trowelled top, laid out in blocks
portland_cement_walk.bound_note: The code's first sidewalk specification (sec. 2062: 'blocks five feet by six feet in size' for 5- and 6-ft walks); the alternatives it allows are limestone (sec. 2068) and cinders between wooden curbs (sec. 2070), and no new wooden walk (sec. 2079). In the Council's proceedings read for this ticket plank walks still outnumber cement ones in 1899 (631 mentions to 453, vol. 43) and cement leads from 1902 (133 to 32 in vol. 49, 236 to 19 in vol. 51), with cinder walks for the outskirts. The c. 1923 views of both Glessner frontages show a pale walk in jointed slabs.

sandstone_curbstone.name: sandstone curbstone
sandstone_curbstone.what: dressed sandstone curbstones set on edge at the outer edge of the sidewalk space
sandstone_curbstone.bound_note: Sec. 2072 asks for 'a substantial curbing of stone or white-oak plank, not less than three inches in thickness'; in 1902 the Board of Local Improvements' full-text ordinances name 'sandstone curbstones' and name a concrete curb and gutter in the title when they order one, and Prairie Avenue's 1903 title names neither. The c. 1923 views show a pale curb jointed in straight lengths.

grass_plat.name: grass plat (mown turf)
grass_plat.what: turf between the walk and the curb, and in the foot inside the walk
grass_plat.bound_note: Sec. 2077's 'courts or open spaces ... for planting trees or for grass plats', which 'shall not be covered with plank or other material'; grass on both Glessner frontages c. 1923.

exists.to_basis: reconstructed: rock asphalt was ordered 11 May 1903 (vol. 51 p. 38), was not down on 2 Nov 1903 (vol. 52) and was down, 'Needs repairs', on 7 Nov 1906 (vol. 58 p. 1932); drawn as it stood before the paving

alley_indiana_prairie_20_21.note: The one alley with a record: 'the north and south alley first west of Prairie avenue, from 20th street to 21st street' was ordered paved with rock asphalt in May 1903 and was paved between November 1903 and November 1906. It is drawn as it stood before, unimproved; it may already have been rock asphalt on 1 July 1904.

exists.from_basis: reconstructed: cement walks lead the Council's sidewalk orders from 1902 (vols. 49-51) and are the code's first specification (sec. 2062)
exists.to_basis: a pale walk in jointed slabs on both Glessner frontages in the c. 1923 views (HABS nos. 2, 3)

walk.blocks_note: Sec. 2062: 'All work on 5, 6, 10, 12 ... foot walks to be laid out in blocks five feet by six feet in size' -- so a 6-ft walk is one 6-ft block across and 5-ft blocks along, and a 5-ft walk the other way about.
walk.note: No record read says what the walks of these blocks were made of in 1904. Cement concrete is what the city was mostly ordering by 1902 and what the c. 1923 photographs show; limestone flagging is the likeliest alternative on an avenue walked since the 1870s, and a plank walk, still common in 1899, the least likely on this one.

exists.from_basis: reconstructed: curbing was let with the district's pavings of 1899-1903 (16th Street, Indiana, 22nd Street, Prairie Avenue)
exists.to_basis: a pale curb jointed in straight lengths on both Glessner frontages c. 1923 (HABS nos. 2, 3)

curb.note: Prairie Avenue 16th-20th was CURBED under the 1903 ordinance; its printed title names no 'combined curb and gutter', which the Board's titles of that year name whenever they order one, and the Board's full-text ordinances of 1902 name sandstone curbstones. So a stone curb is the likelier reading there, and the stone is reconstructed; the cross streets' older macadam may have had white-oak plank, which sec. 2072 also allowed.

exists.from_basis: reconstructed: sec. 2077's grass plats; the avenue described as 'tree lined' in the 1880s (HABS data p. 2, quoting Meeker)
exists.to_basis: grass parkways on both Glessner frontages c. 1923 (HABS nos. 2, 3)

parkway.note: Turf between the walk and the curb. No tree is drawn: trees are not this ticket's.

exists.from_basis: reconstructed: sec. 2062 sets the walk one foot off the lot line and says nothing of the foot
exists.to_basis: a grass strip between the walk and the wall on 18th Street c. 1923 (HABS no. 3)

margin.note: The foot between the lot line and the walk, drawn as turf like the parkway.
